source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The elevation specifically proves a pulmonary cause of dyspnea and therefore excludes clinically important heart failure.","B":"The elevation establishes normal ventricular function because BNP rises only when lung disease is the primary cause of symptoms.","C":"The elevation has no established role in evaluating dyspnea or suspected heart failure and should not affect the assessment.","D":"The elevation supports possible heart failure but is not diagnostic by itself because BNP can also rise in other cardiac and pulmonary conditions."}}
source_row.rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories notes that BNP is useful in evaluating suspected congestive heart failure, while elevated concentrations can also occur in conditions such as right heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, pulmonary embolism and acute coronary syndromes.
